# BH-700 Baghouse Control Narrative (Draft A, for review)

I built this only from Dave's email. Anything the email did not state is marked **Proposed** or listed as an open item in Section 10. Six open items block programming: OI-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, and 07.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

**FR-BH700-001** BH-700 removes dust from kiln exhaust gas. It controls the equipment listed in Section 2.

**Interfaces**

| Interface | Direction | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Kiln feed module (tag TBD) | Out | Kiln feed stop request |
| Kiln ID fan and kiln interlocks | Both | Not defined in the email (OI-09) |
| SIS (if any) | Both | Referenced to the SRS only |

## 2. Equipment and tags

The instrument index is the master list. This table shows only what the email named.

| Tag | Description | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SC-701 | Screw conveyor | Hopper discharge |
| RV-702 | Rotary airlock | Hopper discharge |
| F-703 | ID fan | |
| D-704 | Inlet damper | Fail position TBD (OI-08) |
| TT-705 | Inlet temperature | |
| D-706 | Bleed-air damper | Fail position TBD (OI-08) |
| PDT-7xx | Baghouse DP | Tag not in email (OI-10) |
| Pulse valves, rows 1 to n | Cleaning rows | Tags and row count TBD (OI-10) |

### Setpoint list (single source for all numbers)

| ID | Item | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-BH700-01 | Pulse interval, normal | 10 s per row | Email |
| SP-BH700-02 | Pulse interval, high DP | 5 s per row | Email |
| SP-BH700-03 | DP high (fast pulse on) | 6 to 7 in. (unit assumed in. w.c.) | Email gives a range. Pick one value (OI-06). |
| SP-BH700-04 | DP high return deadband | TBD | Not in email (OI-06) |
| SP-BH700-05 | DP high-high (kiln feed stop) | 8 in. | Email |
| SP-BH700-06 | Delay, F-703 running to D-704 open | 60 s | Email says "a minute or so" (OI-06) |
| SP-BH700-07 | Clean-down duration | 10 min | Email |
| SP-BH700-08 | TT-705 high (open D-706) | 450 °F | Email |
| SP-BH700-09 | TT-705 high return deadband | TBD | Not in email |
| SP-BH700-10 | Step timeouts (start sequence) | TBD | Not in email |
| SP-BH700-11 | Equipment run-out time at stop | TBD | Not in email |

## 3. States and transitions

This table follows ISA-106 state naming. Automation level: **M** manual, **OP** operator-prompted, **A** automatic.

| State | Entry permissive | Allowed exits | Initiator | Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | None (initial state) | STARTING | Operator | OP |
| STARTING | Start permissives met (C&E chart) | RUNNING, HELD, STOPPING, ABORTING | Auto after operator START | A |
| HELD | Step timeout or step failure | STARTING (resume), STOPPING, ABORTING | Auto or operator | OP |
| RUNNING | Start sequence complete | STOPPING, ABORTING | Operator or auto | A |
| STOPPING | Operator STOP | STOPPED, ABORTING | Operator | A |
| ABORTING | RV-702 stopped, or operator ABORT | ABORTED | Auto or operator | A |
| ABORTED | Abort actions complete | STOPPED (after reset) | Operator reset | OP |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-002 | The BPCS shall allow only the transitions in the table above. | FAT: attempt each disallowed transition. |
| FR-BH700-003 | The BPCS shall hold the ABORTED state until the operator resets it and the start permissives are met. | FAT: reset with a permissive false, then true. |

## 4. Regulatory control

BH-700 has no PID loops. The cleaning control is below.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-004 | In RUNNING and STOPPING (clean-down), the BPCS pulses one row at a time in row order. | FAT: observe pulse output order. |
| FR-BH700-005 | The BPCS uses the interval SP-BH700-01 while PDT-7xx is below SP-BH700-03. | FAT: force DP below the setpoint. |
| FR-BH700-006 | The BPCS uses the interval SP-BH700-02 while PDT-7xx is at or above SP-BH700-03. It returns to SP-BH700-01 after DP falls below SP-BH700-03 minus SP-BH700-04. | FAT: ramp DP up and down. |
| FR-BH700-007 | The BPCS requests a kiln feed stop when PDT-7xx reaches SP-BH700-05. **Proposed:** operator-prompted, not automatic (OI-03). | FAT: force DP high-high and check the prompt and the request. |
| FR-BH700-008 | The BPCS opens D-706 when TT-705 reaches SP-BH700-08. It closes D-706 after TT-705 falls below SP-BH700-08 minus SP-BH700-09. | FAT: ramp TT-705 up and down. |

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start (STOPPED to RUNNING)

Timeouts are SP-BH700-10 unless noted.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check start permissives (C&E chart). | All permissives true | SP-BH700-10 | Stay in STOPPED. Show the failed permissive. |
| 2 | Start SC-701. | SC-701 running feedback | SP-BH700-10 | HELD. Alarm. |
| 3 | Start RV-702. | RV-702 running feedback | SP-BH700-10 | HELD. Alarm. |
| 4 | Start F-703. | F-703 running feedback | SP-BH700-10 | HELD. Alarm. |
| 5 | Wait for the fan-to-damper delay. | SP-BH700-06 elapsed | n/a | n/a |
| 6 | Open D-704. | D-704 open feedback | SP-BH700-10 | HELD. Alarm. |
| 7 | Start pulsing (Section 4). | Pulse timer active | SP-BH700-10 | HELD. Alarm. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-009 | The BPCS runs steps 1 to 7 in order. | FAT: run the sequence. |
| FR-BH700-010 | **Proposed:** Start SC-701 before RV-702, so the downstream equipment runs first (OI-01). | FAT: check start order. |
| FR-BH700-011 | The email says the fan may start before SC-701 and RV-702 ("either works"). The BPCS does not support this order until OI-01 closes. | Review: OI-01 closed. |

### 5.2 Stop with clean-down (RUNNING to STOPPED)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Send the kiln feed stop request. **Proposed** (OI-04). | Request sent | n/a | Alarm. Continue. |
| 2 | Keep F-703, SC-701, and RV-702 running. Keep pulsing. **Proposed** (OI-05). | SP-BH700-07 elapsed | n/a | n/a |
| 3 | Stop pulsing. | Pulse output off | SP-BH700-10 | Alarm. Continue. |
| 4 | Stop F-703. Close D-704. **D-704 position during clean-down: OI-05.** | F-703 stopped feedback | SP-BH700-10 | Alarm. Go to ABORTING. |
| 5 | Run RV-702 and SC-701 for SP-BH700-11. Then stop both. | Both stopped feedback | SP-BH700-10 | Alarm. Show to operator. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-012 | The BPCS keeps F-703 running and pulsing for SP-BH700-07 after a normal STOP. | FAT: stop and time the clean-down. |
| FR-BH700-013 | An operator ABORT during clean-down moves BH-700 to ABORTING. | FAT: abort in step 2. |

### 5.3 Abort on airlock stop

The email says to shut down quickly when the airlock stops, because the hopper fills. The 2019 fire is the design basis. The actions below are **Proposed** (OI-02).

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-014 | When RV-702 stops while BH-700 is not STOPPED, the BPCS moves to ABORTING. This is not a normal stop. | FAT: trip RV-702 in each state. |
| FR-BH700-015 | In ABORTING, the BPCS stops pulsing and stops F-703. It closes D-704, stops SC-701, and sends the kiln feed stop request. It does not run clean-down. | FAT: check every output after the trip. |
| FR-BH700-016 | The ABORTING actions run with no operator input and no step delay. | FAT: measure the time from trip to last output. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

The cause-and-effect chart (BH-700-CE, to be created) is the master. Do not restate the logic here. The email adds these rows:

| C&E row | Cause | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| CE-BH700-01 | RV-702 stopped | Abort (FR-BH700-014, -015) |
| CE-BH700-02 | PDT-7xx at SP-BH700-05 | Kiln feed stop prompt (FR-BH700-007) |
| CE-BH700-03 | TT-705 at SP-BH700-08 | Open D-706 (FR-BH700-008) |
| CE-BH700-04 | Start permissives | Start sequence step 1 (list TBD, OI-10) |

The email gives no hopper high level, no fire or CO detection, and no high-high temperature. The hopper-fill fire risk may need an SIS function. Decide this in the hazard review (OI-07). Reference any SIS function to the SRS. Do not specify it here.

## 7. Alarms

The rationalized alarm database is the master. These entries are needed from the email. Priority and setpoints belong in the database.

| Alarm | Source |
|---|---|
| Baghouse DP high | SP-BH700-03 |
| Baghouse DP high-high | SP-BH700-05 |
| Inlet temperature high | SP-BH700-08 |
| RV-702 stopped (abort) | CE-BH700-01 |
| Start sequence HELD, with step number | Section 5.1 |
| Bad PV: PDT-7xx, TT-705 | Section 8 |

## 8. Abnormal handling

All responses are **Proposed**. The email does not cover this section (OI-08).

| Condition | Required response |
|---|---|
| PDT-7xx bad PV | Use the interval SP-BH700-02. Alarm. Do not issue a kiln feed stop request on bad quality. |
| TT-705 bad PV | Treat as high. Open D-706. Alarm. |
| Comms loss to a drive | Treat as that drive stopped. For RV-702, go to ABORTING. |
| Comms loss to the kiln feed module | Alarm. Prompt the operator to stop kiln feed by hand. |
| Power loss and restart | All drives stay stopped. BH-700 starts in STOPPED. The operator starts it again. |
| Fail positions | D-704 fails closed. D-706 fails open. Confirm both in the hazard review. |

## 9. Operator interface

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Faceplate | BH-700 state, start step, and clean-down time remaining |
| Operator commands | START, STOP, ABORT, RESET |
| Operator changes | None. Setpoints are engineer-level. |
| Prompts | Kiln feed stop at DP high-high. HELD with the failed step. |
| Indicators | Pulse interval in use, DP, TT-705, and the status of SC-701, RV-702, F-703, D-704, D-706 |

Operations must sign off on states and prompts.

## 10. Open items

Owners are by role, because the email names no one else. Due dates are proposed.

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Choose one start order. Dave says "either works". Mike prefers the fan first to prevent bag blinding. Decide if the fan-first order is needed and its permissives. | Shift supervisor, with Controls lead | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-02 | Confirm the abort actions for an airlock stop, and how quickly each must complete. | Process engineer | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-03 | Decide if the kiln feed stop at DP high-high is automatic or operator-prompted. Dave says "usually". | Shift supervisor | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-04 | Confirm the kiln feed stop request on a normal stop. | Process engineer | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-05 | Define clean-down: D-704 position, whether SC-701 and RV-702 keep running, the pulse interval, and the run-out time SP-BH700-11. | Process engineer | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-06 | Fix single values for SP-BH700-03, -04, -06, and -09. Confirm the DP unit. | Shift supervisor | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-07 | Hazard review of the 2019 hopper fire. Decide on hopper level, fire detection, and a high-high temperature action. Decide which functions go in the SRS. | Process safety lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-08 | Confirm the Section 8 responses and the fail positions of D-704 and D-706. | Controls lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-09 | Define the kiln interface (kiln feed module tag, kiln interlocks, and ID fan interaction). | Controls lead | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-10 | Add missing tags (PDT-7xx, pulse valves, row count) and the start permissive list to the instrument index. Create the C&E chart. | Integrator | 2026-11-08 |

## Checks

- Numbers appear only in the setpoint list. Prose cites the IDs.
- Every requirement has an ID and a test method.
- Every state has entry permissives and exits.
- Every start and stop step has a timeout and failure response. The values are TBD under SP-BH700-10.
- Bad PV, comms loss, power loss, and fail positions are defined, as proposals.
- Not done: the STE editing pass is not final. Section 9 and the open item text need a second pass after the content is settled.
